To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

PDGF‐AB stimulates SMC proliferation through activation of MEK and that the MEK1 inhibitors, UO126 and UO126, block PDGF‐Ab induced phosphorylation of MEKS at threonine 293 in porcine aortic smooth muscle cells.
MEK1/MEK2 inhibitors UO 126 and PD980059 block PDGF‐ab induced phosphorylation of Thr 292 and increase phosphorylation at Ser 218/222 in porcine vascular smooth muscle cells (SMC).

the MEK1 inhibitors PD98059/UO126 block PDGF‐induced phosphorylation of Thr 292 in MEK1 and that the MEK inhibitor‐induced hyperphosphorylated MEK1 is not active and therefore inhibits SMC proliferation.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the question of how GFs stimulate SSMC proliferation.
a new mechanism by which MEK1/MEK2 inhibitors block SMC proliferation and arteriogenesis.
the molecular regulation of arteriogenesis and the identification of potential therapeutic targets.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
GF‐induced MEK1 phosphorylation is not only a “on” signal but also a “stop” signal.

the MEK1 inhibitor UO126 inhibits MEK1/Thr292 phosphorylation, which in turn leads to an increase in phosphorylation of MEk1/2 at the Ser218/222 site, which in turn inhibits the phosphorylation of ERK1/2 and thus inhibits cell proliferation.
the MEK1 inhibitors PD98059 or UO126 inhibit PDGF‐AB‐induced SMC proliferation by blocking phosphorylation of Thr 292 and by hyperphosphorylating Ser218/222.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
GFs stimulate cell cycle progression via MEK1/ 2 phosphorylation at Ser218/ 222 and that the inhibitors block this process via inhibition of phosphorylation of Thr 292.
the inhibition of MEK1 by UO126 or PD98059 leads to hyperphosphorylated MEK1/Thr292 which is unable to be activated.
the inhibition of SMC proliferation by UO126 or PD98059 depends on the phosphorylated status of MEK1.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the phosphorylation status of MEK1 in response to PDGF‐AB is more complex than previously anticipated.
MEK1/MEK2 inhibitors UO 126 and PD980 59 are not suitable for inhibition of MEK1 in SMC and that the mechanism of inhibition of MEK inhibitors needs to be reconsidered.
the MEK1 inhibitors PD98059, UO126 and others do not inhibit SMC proliferation by inhibiting MEK1/MEK2 but rather by inhibiting the activation of MEK2 by MEK1.
